I have a master's degree in AI. These days I'm an ML/AI engineer at an AI startup, building generative AI products.

Building products is fun, and I like it. It also pulls me away from research, and I miss that. This site is where I keep the research side going: I read papers closely, run small analyses and side projects, and write down what I learned. Most of it is about image generation.

The notes are of three kinds. *Fundamentals* go back to the foundational papers and connect them. *Paper reviews* take a recent paper and look at what its results actually support. *Experiments* are small runs to check a claim or a method, including the ones that went nowhere. Topics are tags on each note.

If a note was useful to you, or you find a mistake in one, I'd be glad to hear about it. [Email me](mailto:{{< var email >}}). New notes go out through the [RSS feed](notes.xml); code and figure sources are on [GitHub](https://github.com/gs3393).
